findings.rule: Rollback doc accuracy: it must name every request path that the table drop breaks
findings.trigger: The same commit (dc28a7c) made unlockApplication write a ledger row (wallet.ts:214), but the doc still says that dropping the table under this image breaks only new-wallet creation and purchase grants. An operator follows the doc and does a single-deploy DROP during a quiet window, expecting existing users to be unaffected. Instead, every existing user's first-time POST /applications/X/unlock fails with 42P01 and answers 500, and that is the paid core action.
findings.title: The rollback doc leaves out unlock: after the table drop, every new unlock also answers 500, not only new wallets and purchases
findings.proof: In the drop test (ledger test:528), after the DROP, call POST /v1/tailormyresume/applications/another-app/unlock for 'dropper' and observe a 500. Fix the doc sentence (and the PR body) to read 'new-wallet creation, purchase grants and unlocks'.

findings.rule: History order: GET /credits is sorted by created_at, then id (ledger.ts:54-57); the export is oldest first
findings.trigger: A new user's first request is POST /applications/X/unlock. ensureWallet (line 176) writes WELCOME +1, and line 214 writes TAILORING -1, in the same transaction. created_at defaults to now(), which is the transaction start (0008), so both rows get the same timestamp. The tie-break is the random v4 uuid id. In about half of cases, the oldest-first export and GET /credits put the -1 spend before the +1 grant, so a running balance shows -1.
findings.title: WELCOME and TAILORING rows from one first-unlock transaction share created_at and are ordered by a random uuid
findings.proof: Run a loop of 20 fresh users, each with only POST unlock and then GET /credits. Assert that entries[0].kind === 'TAILORING' every time. It fails on some runs. Fix: set createdAt to sql`clock_timestamp()` in recordLedger (ledger.ts:32-34).
